title: Data Preparation Guide
text: jtbdtools requires specific column naming format: Rules: Prefix: imp__ importance, sat__ satisfaction (double underscore) Job step objective separated . (period) spaces anywhere name importance column must matching satisfaction column Data must factor format levels 1-5

title: Data Preparation Guide
text: data SPSS format (.sav):
code: library(haven) library(labelled)  # Import df_spss <- haven::read_sav("your_survey.sav")  # Inspect labels dictionary <- labelled::generate_dictionary(df_spss)

title: Data Preparation Guide
text: build_imp_column_names() build_sat_column_names() functions handle SPSS data follows standard survey instrument format: : Swap SPSS labels column names Remove prefix (--) Remove suffix (-) Replace spaces underscores Add imp__/sat__ prefix job section Convert labelled data factors
code: DistinctQuestionId_Question_Text - How Important... DistinctQuestionId_Question_Text - How Satisfied... library(jtbdtools)  # Separate importance and satisfaction columns first df_imp <- df_spss[, imp_column_indices] df_sat <- df_spss[, sat_column_indices]  # Rename with job section df_imp_renamed <- build_imp_column_names(df_imp, "researching") df_sat_renamed <- build_sat_column_names(df_sat, "researching")  # Combine df_ready <- cbind(df_imp_renamed, df_sat_renamed)

title: Data Preparation Guide
text: data isn’t SPSS format, rename columns manually:
code: library(dplyr)  df <- your_data %>%   rename(     imp__researching.minimize_time_to_find_options = q1_importance,     sat__researching.minimize_time_to_find_options = q1_satisfaction,     imp__researching.minimize_time_to_evaluate_options = q2_importance,     sat__researching.minimize_time_to_evaluate_options = q2_satisfaction   ) %>%   mutate(across(starts_with("imp__"), ~ factor(., levels = 1:5))) %>%   mutate(across(starts_with("sat__"), ~ factor(., levels = 1:5)))

title: Data Preparation Guide
text: Invisible characters: SurveyMonkey exports sometimes include Unicode -break spaces (U+00A0) instead regular spaces. invisible Excel cause column matching fail. Factor levels: Columns must factors levels 1-5, numeric character. Matching pairs: Every imp__ column must exactly matching sat__ column (job step objective name).

title: Introduction to jtbdtools
text: Jobs---Done (JTBD) theory says customers “hire” products get job done. Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI), developed Tony Ulwick, turns quantitative framework: survey users important outcome satisfied current solutions, calculate biggest gaps . opportunity score formula: importance exceeds satisfaction, gap amplifies opportunity. satisfaction exceeds importance, opportunity equals importance (floor). Scores range 0-20, anything 10 considered high-opportunity outcome.

title: Quantitative Jobs-to-Be-Done Analysis Using Outcome-Driven Innovation
text: Based Tony Ulwick’s Outcome-Driven Innovation. package: Converts Likert-scale (1-5) survey responses 0-10 scores using top-2-box scoring (% rating 4 5) Applies ODI formula: opportunity = importance + max(0, importance - satisfaction) Compares scores across user segments identify specific groups underserved Generates publication-ready visualizations tables
